cards.explanation: The answer is land. On the fourteenth night, about midnight, the sailors sensed they were approaching land. I think those sailors perked up faster than I do when the oven timer dings. After fourteen nights of being driven across the sea, friends, that's news.

The answer is fifteen. The first reading was twenty fathoms, then they went a little farther and got fifteen. Right after that, fearing they would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern.

The answer is True. Fearing they would run aground on the rocks, the sailors dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak. Notice they put the anchors down first and asked for morning second. Four anchors in the dark and a prayer for light, friends, and I'd have done the exact same thing.

The answer is the lifeboat. The sailors were pretending to lower anchors from the bow, but what they let down into the sea was the lifeboat. That's the sneaky part, friends. They looked busy with the anchors while they were really trying to escape.

The answer is that if they leave, you cannot be saved. Paul told the centurion, the Roman officer in charge, and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.” (Acts 27:31) He caught the plan and went straight to the people who could stop it. I think that's some quick thinking from a man who had been in a storm for two weeks.

The answer is that they cut the ropes and let it drift. Snip, snip, and off it floats. Paul had just told the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.” Then the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.

The answer is eat. Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat. He told them, “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.” (Acts 27:33) Fourteen days without food, and here's a man saying, come on, have something.

The answer is True. Paul says, “…not a single hair of your head will be lost.” (Acts 27:34) He says it right after urging them to eat something for their own preservation. A promise like that is a lot to hand a hungry crew in a storm.

The answer is False. The text says, “They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.” (Acts 27:36) They saw Paul give thanks to God over the bread and start eating. After that, the whole ship joined in.

The answer is throwing the grain into the sea. Overboard goes the grain, friends. After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea. Eat first, then lighten the load, and that's the order the text gives.

The answer is to run the ship aground there. When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could. Notice the "…if they could." I think they were hoping it would work.

The answer is False. The ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves. They aimed for the beach, but a sandbar got in the way first.

The answer is swim. The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom. It's a heavy moment, so I'll say it plainly: this plan was a real threat to Paul and the others. Swimming turns out to matter again in the very next verses.

The answer is that he wants to spare Paul's life. That's the reason the text gives: the centurion, wanting to spare Paul's life, thwarted their plan. One officer stepped in and stopped it. I think Paul was glad he did.
The answer is True. The centurion commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land. I think that was a smart order. The rest were to follow after that.

The answer is on planks and parts of the ship. The text says the rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. Pieces of a ship that was breaking up became their way to land, and I'd have held on to mine with my mustache wrapped around it.

The answer is True. There were 276 on board, and the text says, “In this way everyone was brought safely to land.” (Acts 27:44) That's the same promise Paul made earlier about not losing a single hair (Acts 27:34). Every last one of them made it, friends.
